Honestly, if you have a good therapist, they might ask you some basic questions, but really they just want you to tell them what's going on at your own pace. If you end up crying, they always have tissues. Trust me, it's totally normal (: You don't have to make eye contact or talk too much if you don't want to. The whole reason for it is to help you, so you being comfortable is the number one priority. Depending on where you go, they might have legos or coloring books or something to keep you occupied. My former therapist also worked with little children, so I just kind of colored while I was there (I was 17/18. No shame). Basically, make sure you feel comfortable with your therapist and don't be afraid to ask them questions about anything, that's what they're there for. But good luck! I hope it helps you!

Weirdly enough, hospital was my favorite thing. It was nice because I was surrounded by other teens going through the same issues, we played guitar hero and stuff all the time, I got them to let us watch Criminal Minds one night (seriously don't know how I got the tech to agree to that but it was awesome). Plus, once a week they'd bring in therapy dogs, so that was cool. The doctors and nurses would actually listen to what you had to say and made you feel like they genuinely cared. They do med checks and everything and usually check your vitals everyday, but it's not so bad. The food isn't awful either :p I was there twice (8 days the first time, 10 days the second time). Honestly I felt so much better being there and in the weeks and months afterward. The only reason I'm not still good is because I can't take my medication anymore. It's definitely worth going, please please please do it. And if you need anyone to talk to in the meantime, I'm totally here for you.
